label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Hi Mr. Bergeron, and everyone,

You are right to ask for a straight answer, so here it is: **Pétrin Doré is not closing or moving. I bought the building!**

I wanted to keep it a surprise until the reopening, but after seeing this thread I understand why people were worried. We have all seen too many small shops disappear from Mile End. I should have explained the sign better.

Marc-Antoine, your cousin is half right: the building was sold. But it was sold to me! M. Ferland, who owns it, is 81 and is retiring to Sherbrooke to be closer to his daughter. He offered to sell it to me before offering it to anybody else, and we signed at the notary on December 15.

M. Ferland has come in almost every morning for 17 years for his baguette *pas trop cuite*. He cried a little at the notary, and I think I did too. It means a lot to me that he trusted me with the building.

**About the carnets: every one is still good. There is no expiry date.** We sold 214 of them in October, at $60 for 12 loaves, and we will honour every loaf. Noodle_and_crumb, your seven loaves are waiting for you. We will also give each carnet holder a free croissant in January.

And if anybody would really prefer their money back for their carnet, please come and see me. I will give it back, no questions asked. I do not want anyone feeling uncomfortable about it.

I have to say, seeing the word “scam” hurt after 17 years on this street. But I understand that with a vague sign and news that the building was sold, people had questions. I hope this clears it up.

We will be **closed January 4 to 18 for work and will reopen Tuesday, January 19 at 7:00 a.m.** We are getting a new four-deck oven from a supplier in Laval. The old oven is from 1998 and broke down three times this year, so it is more than ready for retirement too.

We are also taking the space at the back that used to be the dépanneur’s storage. We will have six small tables. Finally, you can sit down with your coffee and bread instead of trying to balance everything outside!

And for anyone worried about the people who live upstairs: **the three apartments will stay rented, with the same tenants and the same rent.** I have promised them this in writing.

As for the sign, my nephew Thomas wrote it at six in the morning. “Grande nouvelle” was his idea, and I said yes without thinking about how it would sound. I think we have both learned something! The half-empty shelves on the 28th had nothing to do with closing, either. We had sold everything for Christmas Eve, including 400 bûches.

To celebrate, please come by on **Saturday, January 23**. Everyone is invited for a free coffee and a piece of the new bread. I would love to see you there and show you the new space.

Thank you, Priya, for your kind words, and thank you to everyone who stood up for us and everyone who has supported us since we opened at 5 rue Fairmount in March 2009. Your concern means you care about this little bakery, and that means a great deal to me.

See you soon,
Hélène
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré
